# This repository calls no PR baseline, so its PR bodies are unchecked

## Context

Relocated from `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#46`, which I filed an hour earlier and am closing in favour of this. Not a duplicate — the same leaf in the repository where the work lands and where the gate that governs it lives. The move is forced by evidence, and the evidence is the point:

**The Engine's PR-body lint requires a bare, standalone `Resolves #N` and rejects a qualified cross-repo close target.** Measured — the restored gate failed PR #18270 on its first run with exactly that:

```
❌ Agent PR body is missing required template anchors.
   First missing: `Resolves #N` on its own line (mandatory closing keyword —
   `Refs`/`Related` alone is not sufficient …)
```

The PR body carried `Resolves neomjs/neo-agent-skills#46`. So a consumer-caller leaf tracked in the Skills repo **cannot be closed by the PR that implements it**, because this repository's own gate will not accept the reference. `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#40` — the Brain's equivalent leaf — will hit this identically the moment someone implements it. Flagged to @neo-gpt-emmy, who owns the governance epic.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 20 open issues in `neomjs/neo` at 2026-09-04T11:2xZ; no equivalent. `#17783` is adjacent and explicitly routes this scope away — *"`neo-agent-skills#14` owns cross-repository callers and required-context binding"* — and it is @neo-gpt's, scoped to R2/R3.
**A2A in-flight claim sweep:** `list_messages({status: 'all', limit: 30})` — no `[lane-claim]` on CI governance or baseline adoption.
**Memory Core rationale sweep:** returned the deleted gate's catch history, recorded under The Problem.
**Own-assignment sweep:** no open assigned ticket of mine covers CI governance.

## The Problem

`neo-agent-skills` publishes `reusable-pr-baseline.yml`, a `workflow_call` workflow owning five guard jobs. Measured on `origin/dev` at 2026-09-04T10:53Z:

```
$ git grep -n "neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows" origin/dev -- .github/
(zero hits)
```

This repository calls it from nowhere, so the `pr-body` job has never run on an Engine PR.

**Not theoretical — a regression of a gate with a measured catch rate.** Until 2026-08-26 this repository ran `agent-pr-body-lint.yml`, deleted in `91ae3604b4` (#17791). Memory Core holds repeated live catches before that: three PR bodies corrected at once for a missing self-identification anchor; a *"seventh recorded hit"* on the same lint with a new failure shape; a red body-lint on PR #14897 that, chased, also surfaced body-vs-branch drift across eleven commits. Since deletion, **nothing** has checked a PR body here, and the failure is silent — nothing red, nothing missing, just an unrun gate.

The paired local half is `neo-agent-skills#24` (`agent-preflight`, Brain-hosted, unreachable from here). Both halves are currently absent for this repository.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Called workflow:** `neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml` — inputs `required_base` (default `dev`), `node_version` (default `24`); no required secrets.
- **Caller obligation, per that file's own header:** the caller owns its trigger, and `types: [opened, edited, synchronize, ready_for_review]` is required. `edited` is load-bearing — the `pr-body` job reads the live body, so a corrected body only re-runs if the caller fires on the edit. A reusable workflow cannot see its caller's `on:` block.
- **Working precedent:** `neomjs/devindex/.github/workflows/shared-pr-baseline.yml`, green since 2026-08-29 — so cross-repo reusable calls are permitted here. **It pins an older two-job version**, so devindex is not getting `pr-body`, `substrate-size` or `source-comment-archaeology` either.
- **Zero `Baseline` runs** in `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-institution`, or `neo-agent-skills` itself.

**Adoption is a consolidation, not an addition** — the reusable workflow exposes no job-selection input, so a caller runs all five:

| baseline job | this repository today | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-base` | `pr-base-guard.yml` | overlap |
| `skills-materialized` | `substrate-sync.yml` is adjacent | uncompared |
| `source-comment-archaeology` | `ticket-archaeology-lint.yml` — **path-scoped**, mirrors `DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS`; the baseline job has no path filter | different scopes, not a superset |
| `substrate-size` | **none** | pure gain — closes the gap carried since `c623b2f63c` |
| `pr-body` | **none** | pure gain |

## The Fix

Add the caller with the required trigger, pinned to an immutable upstream commit. Record each overlap's disposition; delete nothing on an assumed equivalence.

**Measured startup constraint, worth carrying — and my first diagnosis of it was wrong.** A caller granting only `contents: read` produces `startup_failure`: no jobs, no logs, no annotations. A called job cannot request more permissions than its caller grants, and the baseline's `pr-body` job declares `pull-requests: read` because it fetches the pull request itself, so GitHub rejects the whole call before any job starts. **Grant `contents: read` plus `pull-requests: read`.**

I originally attributed this to a workflow-level `concurrency:` block, on the strength of a "minimal caller" that dispatched all five jobs. That experiment dropped `concurrency` AND `permissions` together, so it narrowed the cause to a set of two and I named one of them; the next push falsified it. `neomjs/devindex`'s green caller reinforced the error — it runs on `contents: read` alone because it pins an older baseline with **zero** `pr-body` jobs, making it a precedent for the `uses:` coordinate and no evidence at all about permissions. `concurrency` is still omitted below, on its own merits: it is unnecessary on a caller whose only job is a `uses:`.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. Adopts an already-selected split.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a caller workflow invokes `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` with `types` including `opened`, `edited`, `synchronize`, `ready_for_review`. Evidence: `git grep "neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows"` returning non-zero where it returned zero.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the five `baseline / *` jobs appear in `gh pr checks` on a real PR. **Already observed:** run `33865960472` dispatched all five.
- [x] **AC-3** — red-first on the live PR: a body missing a required anchor makes `baseline / PR body` fail, and correcting it via `gh pr edit` turns it green **with no push**. **Fully observed** on head `468a374ce0`: four runs on one unchanged SHA — success, success, **failure** (standalone `Resolves` removed), success (restored). Only `baseline / PR body` reddened; every sibling job stayed green, so the signal is scoped rather than a blanket re-run. This is what proves the `edited` trigger is wired, the one obligation the reusable workflow cannot self-check.
- [ ] **AC-4** — each of the three overlapping jobs has a recorded disposition: the superseded local workflow is deleted, or the reason it stays is written down. A census, not a spot-check.
- [x] **AC-5** — `substrate-size` reports on Engine PRs. **Observed** green on run `33865960472` and every run since. It has only been shown to PASS; a PR touching a budgeted file is still needed to prove it can fail, which is Post-Merge Validation rather than an open AC. Note the layer: this restores a REPORTING check. `dev` carries no `required_status_checks` rule, so binding it as a merge gate stays with #17783 / neo-agent-skills#14.
- [ ] **AC-6** — `neo-agent-skills#24`'s stale premise is corrected (it claims the hosted half was restored by #17917, which never merged). **Done** at `IC_kwDOUEM8o88AAAABSiyxDA`.

## Out of Scope

- What the five guards check — `neo-agent-skills` `#15`, `#18`, `#25`, `#28`/`#29`.
- The Brain's caller — `neo-agent-skills#40`.
- `neo-agent-skills#24`'s doc fix. This makes that fix statable; it does not perform it.
- Changing `reusable-pr-baseline.yml`, including adding job-selection inputs or teaching its `pr-body` job to accept cross-repo close targets. The latter is real and now demonstrated, but it is an upstream change, not a consumer leaf.
- Re-pinning mechanics — `neo-agent-skills#38`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Restoring `agent-pr-body-lint.yml` here.** Exactly what #17917 attempted and @tobiu rejected: a per-repository restoration of governance five-plus repositories need identically.
- **Adding the caller and leaving the three local workflows silently in place.** Two guards per concern with no stated owner; the next divergence between them is silent.
- **Deleting `ticket-archaeology-lint.yml` as superseded.** It is path-scoped and the baseline job is not — different scopes, and the scope a guard is given is the blind spot it creates.
- **Treating this as one-line work.** The file is short; the disposition of three live workflows in the main repository is not.
